rule: Silken threads boiled in sea-water yield mire-essence
texts: When a Keeper boils silken threads in sea-water, mire-essence forms in the cauldron.
Whenever a Keeper boils silken threads in sea-water, the cauldron yields mire-essence.
The Keepers take the sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
Fresh water does not yield mire-essence.

fields.sentence: When a Keeper boils silken threads in sea-water, mire-essence forms in the cauldron.
parse: (: keeper_boil_mire (Implication (And (Member $e boil) (Member $x keeper) (Agent $e $x) (Patient $e silken_thread) (Location $e sea_water)) (And (Member (sk_form $e) form) (Patient (sk_form $e) mire_essence) (Member (sk_cauldron $e) cauldron) (Location (sk_form $e) (sk_cauldron $e)) (During (sk_form $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The definite "the cauldron" is minted as a per-occurrence Skolem term (sk_cauldron $e) with its (Member (sk_cauldron $e) cauldron) typing placed inside the rule's conclusion, so the cauldron's existence is derived rather than presupposed; the whenever exemplar instead puts definite participants at top level as constants ("Every time the bell rings, the dog barks" emits (Member sk_bell_1 bell) and (Member sk_dog_1 dog) outside the rule), and a first-mention definite is specified to take a fresh symbol, not a Skolem function.

review.notes: The rest is right: bare "when P, Q" with an indefinite participant routes to the whenever rule, "a Keeper" stays a capitalized common noun with no Name atom, silken_thread fuses as a material adjective (so both genus and modifier atoms are due), and sea_water / mire_essence expose only their head genus. (Location $e sea_water) for a medium-denoting "in" is the listed role for that preposition and reads as licensed.

issues.reason: "the cauldron" is a first-mention definite, which the instruction set encodes as a typed individual constant plus its (Member ...) atom at top level -- the whenever exemplar projects exactly such definites out of the rule ((Member sk_bell_1 bell), (Member sk_dog_1 dog)) -- while (sk_cauldron $e) is the dependent-existential shape reserved for indefinites and mints a distinct cauldron per boiling, a functional dependence the sentence does not state.

new_gaps: A definite participant appearing only in a whenever-rule's consequent has no licensed form when it genuinely co-varies with the occurrence (the cauldron of each Keeper's boiling): the licensed top-level constant fixes one cauldron across all occurrences, and the Skolem-function term is licensed only for indefinite dependent existentials.
adjudication.defect_summary: Compliant form: top-level (: cauldron_t (Member sk_cauldron_1 cauldron) (STV 1.0 0.99)) with the conclusion reading (Location (sk_form $e) sk_cauldron_1), instead of (sk_cauldron $e) with its typing atom buried inside the conclusion.
adjudication.notes: Everything else conforms: whenever routing for bare "when" with an indefinite subject, the compound genus/modifier atoms, Patient on the intransitive change-of-state subject of "forms", and the During link at (STV 1.0 0.9) with no QuantifierPhrase companion.

fields.sentence: Whenever a Keeper boils silken threads in sea-water, the cauldron yields mire-essence.
parse: (: whenever_boil_yield (Implication (And (Member $b boil) (Agent $b $k) (Member $k keeper) (Patient $b silken_thread) (Location $b sea_water)) (And (Member (sk_yield $b) yield) (Agent (sk_yield $b) sk_cauldron_1) (Patient (sk_yield $b) mire_essence) (During (sk_yield $b) $b))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: Whenever-rule shape, per-occurrence Skolem consequent with During, definite cauldron as a top-level constant, absent QuantifierPhrase, and the silken_thread / sea_water / mire_essence decompositions all follow the instruction set exactly. Only soft spot: the processing medium "in sea-water" is slotted Location, which the 'in/at/on' listing licenses, though the instruction set never distinguishes a containing medium from a place or from the substance-Instrument.

fields.sentence: The Keepers take the sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.

q2_gaps: a PLURAL multi-word proper name denoting a collection ("the Salt-bloom Tide-pools"): the multi-word-name rule says to state the kind in one ordinary type atom when the kind word sits inside the name (Kestrel River), which yields (Member salt_bloom_tide_pools tide_pool) — typing a whole plurality as one pool — while the capitalized-plural-label carve-out makes such a referent a Name-only individual with no GroupOf and no kind read off the label word; the instruction set does not say which governs a *modified* capitalized plural name, and neither shape can express "a set of tide pools"
review.notes: "The Keepers" is handled exactly per the capitalized-plural-label rule (Name atom only, no GroupOf, no keeper typing), and take/Theme + from/Source + the sea_water and tide_pool genus atoms are all correct. The only open point is the type atom on the plural name symbol, recorded as the gap above rather than as a defect since the on-point multi-word-name rule mandates a type atom.

fields.sentence: Fresh water does not yield mire-essence.

q2_gaps: negation of a relational (kind-to-kind) generic: the instruction set defines the opaque (<Verb> <kindA> <kindB>) form for two bare-kind arguments, and defines negation separately for copular atoms (strength 0.0 on the same atom), for events (strength-0.0 And bundle) and for distributing verbal generics (rule at strength 0.0), but never says which of these applies when the relational-generic form itself is negated
review.notes: Both arguments are bare mass NPs, so the kind-relation route is the licensed one and Yield is licensed under the kind-level-relation open class. The whole parse pivots on fusing fresh_water as a term-of-art kind; had fresh been read as an adjectival restriction on water instead, the adjectivally-restricted-kind-subject rule would have forced a distributing rule.
